method: Read AGENTS.md and restricted all implementation references to this clean-room checkout. No archived/sibling source or old implementation was inspected.

Read all 17 src/core and 13 src/gateway production files, all 16 scripts code files plus scripts/RELEASE-PREFLIGHT.md, and all three .github workflows. Followed functional callers and recovery boundaries, not only the current diff.

Freshly enumerated all 82 files using Git tracked plus nonignored untracked paths; hashed raw bytes and executable bits. Pinned Node --check parsed all 76 TS/MJS files without executing them; Python ast.parse parsed both Python scripts. Enumerated literal imports and resolved every relative import against current files. This is not typechecking or a compiler dependency graph.

All 32 tests received current structure, declarations and coverage mapping. Nine named test files received current body/assertion review, with additional targeted HTTP/authentication assertion reads. Did not claim every unchanged test assertion was freshly read line-by-line.

Independently traced this change set: bounded history-conversion error metadata, durable not_sent replay and unchanged unknown/no-replay behavior; reviewed all new real WorkerClient/Dispatcher/Ledger consent tests. Reused the already-inspected 54/54 author result without rerunning it.

Verified newly introduced native thread-list coverage remains in the independent official CLI requirement list; assessed its selector/full-plan implications without executing any test selection or full suite.

Rehashed every scoped file and the conversion review dependencies before report publication. No source edits, test runs, network requests, production actions or credentials were performed during this review.
conclusions: Single-administrator setup/login/session/CSRF/owner admission and asynchronous revocation checks remain consistent across HTTP, WebSocket and actual worker/manager write boundaries. Public proof is nonce/origin-bound and does not grant a session.

Durable receipt identity/digest/scope, response minimization and capacity commitments preserve accepted versus not_sent versus unknown. Existing IDs are read before dispatch; lost or malformed positive results cannot authorize replays. Consent-required details are exact primitive whitelist metadata, not history or credentials.

Emergency recovery retains its independent bounded manager slot, actual-child-close slot lifetime, generation fences and maintenance owner tokens. It can preempt worker configuration while preserving root configuration and receipt-rotation exclusivity; no generic journal flag deletion or old-input retry was introduced.

Automation scheduling, unknown-run recovery, workspace witness acknowledgement, worktree registration and receipt export/rotation remain tied to durable positive evidence with bounded resource retention. DST/missed-window behavior and original dispatch identity are explicit.

CI and release tools require exact source/base/head authorization and retain real per-case, per-platform identities. Skipped cases need complementary passing coverage; failures, absent evidence and Go build/probe gaps cannot become green reconciliation. Pinned dependencies, official CLI preparation and isolated homes remain explicit.

Source/history scanners retain full-byte scanning and redacted diagnostics with exact historical exceptions; fresh current bytes are not silently exempt. Builtin MCP public freshness checks remain separate from offline tests and require source-bound evidence; this review does not substitute for the parent final freshness invocation.
adjacentFindingBoundary: A separate reviewer reported missing modelProviders:[] in runtime thread/agents/list. That runtime workflow lies outside this 82-file scope; its author repair and independent closure remain separately owned. This report does not declare all listing/runtime behavior clean.
limits: This is a current exact-scope review, not a newly frozen full-repository audit round, full-suite result, deployment authorization or publication result.
No new runtime behavior or tests were executed. The cited 54/54 is author execution evidence already available and reviewed, not a fresh reviewer run.
No current online service, real inference, external MCP, official freshness network request, Linux/systemd or browser acceptance was performed.
Unchanged test-body review depth is declared per file; syntax/hash inventory is not represented as fresh manual semantic reading of every line.

The separate deployment control report covers 15 files and relies honestly on final matching author/Linux fixture hashes, including retained skips and first failed fixture evidence. thread_history.py itself is independently reviewed by the parent, not included here.
